meta.title: Greece NGO Media — weekly digest
meta.scope: Greece civil society, refugee & humanitarian NGOs, funding and hiring signals (Athens as a common HQ hub)
meta.seoNote: Original desk summaries with links to primary sources. Not a verbatim reprint of publisher content.
meta.disclaimer: Curated digest for orientation. Verify dates and claims on the source pages before acting.

articles.title: ActionAid Hellas opens Community Centre Officer role in Athens
articles.dek: Front-desk, outreach and CRM work at the Athens Community Centre — permanent full-time hire.
body: ActionAid Hellas published a Community Centre Officer vacancy on 26 October, anchored in Athens. The role covers reception, beneficiary engagement, CRM hygiene, daily scheduling and light facilities coordination inside the organisation’s community centre.
The post sits beside ActionAid’s earlier Monitoring & Evaluation Coordinator call (deadline 4 November), signalling a busy HQ hiring window for programme and centre operations staff.
Applicants need a CV (max three pages) and a one-page motivation letter; applications without a letter are excluded. Workable remains the primary ATS.
articles.imageAlt: Team collaborating in a bright office

articles.title: M&E Coordinator hunt continues at ActionAid Hellas
articles.dek: Athens-based monitoring role with a 4 November deadline — data quality, donor reporting, organisational learning.
body: ActionAid Hellas is recruiting a Monitoring and Evaluation Coordinator in Athens, with applications due by 4 November 2026. The brief centres on indicator tracking, data cleaning, dashboards and evidence for donor and internal reports.
Requirements include at least two years in M&E or learning roles in NGO / social-impact settings, plus comfort with tools such as Kobo or similar collection platforms and strong Excel skills.
The opening is a useful barometer for specialised HQ roles in Greece: fewer slots than field caregiving posts, but clearer professional pathways for analysts and MEAL profiles.

articles.title: METAdrasi runs 10th guardianship training for unaccompanied minors
articles.dek: Forty-four mandated persons and temporary representatives joined the seminar — hybrid delivery with state partners.
body: On 21 October METAdrasi hosted its 10th training seminar for Guardianship Mandated Persons and Temporary Representatives of unaccompanied minors. Sessions covered best-interests assessment, the guardianship legal frame, foster care, durable solutions, interpretation and stress management.

Forty-four participants attended in person and online. Speakers included METAdrasi staff plus representatives from the General Secretariat for Vulnerable Persons, Reception and Identification Service, Asylum Service, Dublin Unit and the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family.

Since November 2023 the national guardianship activity has run with METAdrasi as coordinating partner and PRAKSIS as partner, under the Greece AMIF 2021–2027 programme. The seminar underlines how child-protection staffing in Attica remains tightly linked to AMIF-financed pipelines.

articles.title: ARSIS keeps Athens UAM shelters in active recruitment
articles.dek: Educator and caregiving calls for the Athens unaccompanied-minors centre continued through mid/late October.
body: ARSIS posted multiple shelter staffing notices in October, including a full-time Educator role for the Athens Unaccompanied Minors Shelter (call dated 16 October) and rotating / part-time caregiving posts earlier in the month.
Applications typically go to hr.arsis@gmail.com with a CV and interest letter; short contracts with evaluation windows are common under AMIF-backed centre operations.
For jobseekers in Attica, ARSIS remains one of the most visible local publishers of shelter-floor roles — complementary to HOME Project and METAdrasi guardianship pathways.

articles.title: HOME Project seeks part-time morning caregiver in Attica
articles.dek: Early shift (06:00–09:00, six days) with a 30 October deadline — shelters for unaccompanied children.
body: The HOME Project advertised a part-time daily caregiver for Attica, published mid-October with applications closing 30 October 2026. The schedule is a fixed early-morning block six days a week, including weekends and holidays.

HOME Project operates multiple Athens shelters for unaccompanied refugee children with holistic protection services. Clarifications can be sent to hr@homeproject.org up to three days before the deadline.
Together with ARSIS Athens calls, the week’s hiring map shows sustained demand for caregiving capacity in Attica child-protection programmes.

articles.title: MSF: people seeking safety in Greece remain trapped in uncertainty
articles.dek: Psychologists on Lesbos and Samos report re-traumatisation linked to containment, opaque procedures and care gaps.
body: Médecins Sans Frontières published a project update highlighting how deterrence policies, remote closed facilities and fast-track asylum processes deepen psychological distress for people seeking safety in Greece.

MSF psychologists reported more than 900 mental-health consultations on Lesbos and Samos since January 2026, citing barriers to continuous care, limited interpretation for trauma work and the prison-like feel of some reception sites.
The piece remains a key reference for Athens-based advocacy and clinical NGOs tracking island–mainland referral pressure into Attica services.

articles.title: Collective Aid publishes Lesvos summer needs assessment
articles.dek: Shoes, clothing and hygiene top urgent needs; education and safe rest spaces remain scarce.
body: Collective Aid released findings from its Summer 2026 needs assessment with people accessing Parea Community Centre on Lesvos. Respondents most often flagged shoes, clothing and hygiene items as urgent material needs.
Many people described arriving with nothing or only the clothes they wore. Education, private rest spaces and recreational activities ranked among the least available services in the sample.
The assessment is useful reading for mainland NGOs planning in-kind drives or referrals that touch Aegean CCACs and onward movement toward Athens.

articles.title: Amnesty flags trial of human rights defenders Olsen and Dimitras
articles.dek: Charges tied to asylum support and documentation work — Amnesty calls the case a misuse of anti-smuggling law.
body: Amnesty International warned ahead of the Rhodes trial of Tommy Olsen and Panayote Dimitras that criminal charges against the human rights defenders amount to a dangerous conflation of legitimate protection work with smuggling.
The organisation says the pair are targeted for documenting pushbacks and helping people access asylum procedures — activities Amnesty argues are protected human rights work.
The case remains a headline risk indicator for Greek civil society: legal exposure for field documentation can chill NGO operations from the islands to Athens HQ advocacy.

articles.title: EEA Civil Society Fund Greece remains open for CSO proposals
articles.dek: €14.3 million across twelve calls — first wave deadlines cluster in mid-December 2026.
body: The EEA Civil Society Fund Greece, launched in September at the Athens Conservatoire, continues to dominate funding conversations for Greek CSOs. The envelope totals €14.3 million across twelve open grant calls.
Early calls total about €5.1 million with application windows running into mid-December 2026. Themes span civic participation, rights, vulnerable groups and organisational capacity.
For newly forming σωματεία / ΑΜΚΕ in Attica, the fund is one of the clearest near-term institutional routes alongside AMIF project partnerships and private foundations.

articles.title: AMIF Greece calls still shape NGO staffing pipelines
articles.dek: Facilities management and Pact-related administrative actions remain on the TAMΕΥ board with autumn deadlines.
body: The Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF) 2021–2027 Greek programme continues to publish and hold open calls that cascade into NGO and contractor hiring — from facilities management to asylum-system IT and reception health packages.
Notable live items include large facilities-management envelopes and Pact-related capacity actions with deadlines stretching into November–December 2026.
Desk readers tracking Attica jobs should watch AMIF partners (METAdrasi, PRAKSIS, ARSIS, HOME Project and others): public vacancy boards often spike when these grants move into implementation.

articles.title: Synyparxi reports rising Sudanese arrivals seeking aid in Mytilene
articles.dek: Local civil-society initiative sees 100–150 people daily asking for clothes, shoes and food.
body: Aegean media relayed Synyparxi’s alert that daily footfall for basic aid in Mytilene has climbed to roughly 100–150 people in recent weeks, many of them Sudanese nationals seeking clothes, shoes and food.
Volunteer networks are appealing to residents for in-kind support. The pressure on island civil society often foreshadows referral and casework demand toward Athens NGOs weeks later.
For Attica organisations, the story is a reminder that material-aid spikes on Lesvos remain tightly coupled to mainland protection and integration caseloads.

articles.title: Legal-aid capacity for asylum-seekers remains constrained
articles.dek: Guides circulating this month stress early contact with GCR / METAdrasi under UNHCR partnerships — and warn of registration bottlenecks after the EU Pact.
body: Civil-society explainers updated in October reiterate that free asylum legal help in Greece is under strain after funding cuts, while the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum (applicable since mid-June 2026) raises the premium on early advice.
UNHCR’s partnership with Greek Council for Refugees and METAdrasi remains a core NGO channel in Athens, though coverage has narrowed compared with prior years.
Job and volunteer seekers with legal skills should expect high demand and competitive entry into these specialised units.
